fields.summary: OAuth2 clients are not enforcing the PKCE requirement

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: REST API
components.description: All work on the REST API interface

fields.description:
*Description*

MDL-88468 currently allows an administrator to enable PKCE when creating a client. This setting is stored as {{ispkceenabled}} and exposed through {{client_entity::is_pkce_enabled()}}.

However, the authorization flow does not currently use this setting. The {{AuthCodeGrant}} configuration in MDL-88472 also calls:

{noformat}->method('disableRequireCodeChallengeForPublicClients'){noformat}

This disables the League OAuth2 Server library’s default requirement for public clients to provide a code challenge.

As a result, the UI, stored client configuration and authorization behaviour do not currently agree.

This issue should first decide whether Moodle wants to support configurable PKCE. Based on that decision, we should either:

# Keep the PKCE option and implement the corresponding authorization behaviour, including the expected behaviour for public and confidential clients; or
# Remove the PKCE option and its supporting fields from the client management implementation.

If PKCE remains supported, we should also decide:

* whether it is mandatory for public clients;
* whether it is optional or configurable for confidential clients;
* whether both {{plain}} and {{S256}} challenge methods are supported, or only {{S256}}.

*Acceptance criteria*

# The expected PKCE behaviour for public and confidential clients is documented in this issue.
# The client management UI only displays PKCE configuration that is supported by the authorization flow.
# Stored client configuration and authorization behaviour agree.
# If PKCE is required for a client, an authorization request without a valid {{code_challenge}} is rejected.
# When PKCE is used, the token request rejects a missing or invalid {{code_verifier}}.
# Automated tests cover the agreed behaviour for public and confidential clients.
# The behaviour of the following combinations is explicitly tested where applicable:
#* public client without PKCE;
#* public client with valid PKCE;
#* confidential client without PKCE;
#* confidential client with valid PKCE;
#* invalid challenge method;
#* missing or incorrect verifier.

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
*Description:*
When an activity is not yet completed, but is still partially completed, the Activity Completion report tooltip shows "Not completed - Thursday, January 1 1970 1:00:00" (exact time will change depend on timezone). This would be happening due to the value in the timemodified field in the mdl_course_modules_completion table.


While this makes sense at the database level, this information is a source of confusion for Teachers and other users who view the Activity Completion report. At the very least, it should not appear in the UI. At best, it probably shouldn’t appear when downloading the CSV version of the report either, as it is confusing for the average user.


This is replicable in [http://sandbox.moodledemo.net|http://sandbox.moodledemo.net|smart-link]


*Reproduction steps:*

# Create an Assignment activity.
# Enable completion tracking for 'view' and 'make a submission'
# Log in as a student and only view the assignment
# Log in as an admin, go to the Activity Completion report, and hover over the cell.


*Observed*

The "Not completed - Thursday, January 1 1970" date appears in the tooltip:

!image-20260901-014120.png|width=675,alt="image-20260901-014120.png"!


*Expected*
The date does not show when the status is ‘Not completed’ because it provides no relevant information to the user.

fields.summary: React nav: active items in the "More" menu lost their tick and active styling

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
In 5.2 an active item inside the "More" dropdown was shown with a checkmark and the theme's active treatment (dark text on grey, blue on hover/focus). Since the React migration (in MDL-87830) it gets Bootstrap's plain .dropdown-item.active look (blue background, white text) and no checkmark. In MDL-87830 a shared React nav engine was introduced, which is used in both the primary and secondary navigation.

|!custommenu-502.png|width=274,alt="custommenu-502.png"!|!3f240295-2be9-4cbb-a51e-382a6f2ac514.png|width=304,alt="3f240295-2be9-4cbb-a51e-382a6f2ac514.png"!|



*Cause*

Two changes in core/nav/Nav, neither of which the theme rules were updated for:

# Dropdown items render aria-current="page" (Nav.tsx, DropdownItems/DropdownSubmenu) rather than the legacy aria-current="true". Boost's checkmark rules key off [aria-current="true"] / [aria-selected="true"] — see theme/boost/scss/moodle/action-menu.scss and moremenu.scss — so they no longer match.
# Both React mount points deliberately omit the legacy "moremenu" class (primarymoremenu.mustache, secondarymoremenu.mustache), because those rules are written for the legacy <li>-wrapped markup. That also excludes the ".moremenu .dropdown-item.active" treatment (transparent background, body text colour, checkmark, blue on hover/focus-within).

For reference, in 5.2 the .active class on a dropdown item came from moremenu.js's moveIntoMoreDropdown(), which swapped nav-link -> dropdown-item on the moved link and set aria-current="true"; nested submenu children were rendered with aria-current="true" and no .active. React renders that end state directly instead.

*Steps to reproduce*

# Site administration > Appearance > Advanced theme settings, add:
{noformat}Courses|/course/
  -All courses|/course/index.php
  -Course search|/course/search.php{noformat}
# Narrow the browser until "Courses" collapses into the "More" menu.
# Go to /course/search.php, then open "More" > "Courses".

*Expected:* "Course search" (and the "Courses" parent) show a checkmark, as in 5.2.

h2. What is this issue?

Two third-party libraries have a different version pinned in the root {{composer.json}} than the version actually shipped in {{public/lib}} and recorded in {{public/lib/thirdpartylibs.xml}}.

||Package||thirdpartylibs.xml||composer.json / composer.lock||

|{{aws/aws-sdk-php}}|3.369.22|3.356.22|

* {{public/lib/slim/slim/CHANGELOG.md}} - latest entry is 4.15.1
* {{public/lib/aws-sdk/src/Sdk.php:838}} - {{const VERSION = '3.369.22'}}

[MDL-87950|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87950] added all unmodified third-party libraries to {{composer.json}}, pinned at the exact version shipped in Moodle. It landed on 2026-03-04.

* [MDL-86456|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86456] - Upgrade Slim Framework to 4.15.1 (2026-03-12)
* [MDL-87598|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87598] - Upgrade AWS SDK for PHP to 3.369.22 (2026-04-15)

# {{composer.json:81}} - change {{"aws/aws-sdk-php": "3.356.22"}} to {{"3.369.22"}}

fields.summary: Secrets are permanently revoked during client revocation

components.name: REST API
components.description: All work on the REST API interface

fields.description:
Revoking an OAuth2 client currently permanently revokes all associated client secrets which is not a desirable behavior. When an administrator re-enables the client later, those secrets remain permanently revoked and unusable, forcing full re-generation and re-distribution of credentials to external services.

Client revocation should function as an administrative suspension: it must permanently invalidate all active tokens and authorization codes, but preserve secrets so integrations can be temporarily paused and resumed without breaking existing credential configurations.

*Steps to Reproduce*:

# Create an OAuth2 client and generate a client secret.
# Revoke the client.
# Re-enable the client in the administrative interface.
# It’s not possible to authenticate using the original client secret.

*Expected Behavior*:

* *Token Invalidation:* Revoking a client permanently revokes all active access tokens, refresh tokens, and authorization codes.
* *Secret Preservation:* Secrets retain their un-revoked status when the parent client is revoked, but are blocked at runtime while the client is inactive.
* *Secret Status UI:* The secrets management table displays a computed status such as {{Inactive}} with an explanatory notice while the parent client is revoked.
* *Re-enablement:* Re-enabling the client restores functionality to existing active secrets without reviving old tokens.

The reason for this change is that the Client Credentials grant requires no subsequent login step. The client id and secret will allow a client connecting with the client credentials grant *_admin_* access to Moodle.

fields.summary: Inline code text fails colour contrast on every tinted alert background (WCAG 1.4.3)

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
Inline {{<code>}} renders in {{$code-color}} ({{$pink}}, {{#db1a74}}) everywhere. That value clears 4.5:1 on the white page background, but not on any of the pale {{.alert-*}} tints, so any {{<code>}} inside a notification or admin alert falls below the Level AA threshold.

At 14px regular ({{$code-font-size: 87.5%}}) the requirement is 4.5:1.

||Ground||Colour||Ratio||Result||
|{{.alert-danger}}|{{#f4d6d2}}|*3.49:1*|fails|
|{{.alert-primary}}|{{#cfe2f2}}|*3.58:1*|fails|
|{{.alert-success}}|{{#d7e4d6}}|*3.62:1*|fails|
|{{.alert-info}}|{{#cce6ea}}|*3.64:1*|fails|
|{{.alert-warning}}|{{#fcefdc}}|*4.20:1*|fails|
|page background|{{#ffffff}}|4.76:1|passes|
|body grey|{{#f8f9fa}}|4.52:1|passes|

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as an administrator on a site where cron has never run.
# Go to _Site administration > Notifications_.
# Inspect {{admin/cli/cron.php}} inside the "The admin/cli/cron.php script has never been run" warning.

axe-core 4.10.2, run under the same tag set {{behat_accessibility}} uses, reports:

{noformat}color-contrast   serious   1 node
  code
  Element has insufficient color contrast of 4.19
  (foreground #db1a74, background #fcefdc, font size 10.5pt (14px), font weight normal).
  Expected contrast ratio of 4.5:1{noformat}

That page renders only one {{<code>}}, and it happens to sit on the warning tint, which is the mildest of the five. The other four alert variants are worse, down to 3.49:1 on {{alert-danger}}.

h2. Why this is not caught today

{{--bs-code-color}} is a single global, set in {{_root.scss}} from {{$code-color}}, which Boost leaves at {{$pink}}. {{.alert}} already darkens its descendants for contrast, but only for links and the close button:

{noformat}@each $color, $value in $theme-colors {
    .alert-#{$color} {
        a { color: darken(shift-color($value, $alert-color-scale), 10%); }
        .btn-close { color: darken(shift-color($value, $alert-color-scale), 20%); }
    }
}{noformat}

{{code}} is not covered by that loop, so it keeps the global pink.

h2. Suggested fix

Override {{--bs-code-color}} within {{.alert}}, in the same block that already handles {{a}} and {{.btn-close}}. {{darken($code-color, 8%)}} gives {{#b71661}}, the smallest uniform step that clears 4.5:1 on all five tints (worst case 4.66:1 on {{alert-danger}}), and it stays recognisably the same pink. A per-variant value derived from {{$value}}, the way link colours are, would also work and would leave more headroom.

h2. Provenance

Pre-existing rather than introduced in 5.3. {{$pink}} is {{#db1a74}} on 4.5, 5.2 and main; {{$yellow}} is {{#f0ad4e}} on 5.2 and main; and the light mode {{.alert-#{$color}}} block in {{theme/boost/scss/moodle/core.scss}} is identical between 5.2 and main, which only adds dark mode branches to it.

h2. Scope

The measurements above are for {{<code>}} inside alerts, which is what was verified on a running site. The underlying problem is that {{$code-color}} has only 0.26 of headroom on white, so it will fail on any tinted ground. Other tinted surfaces such as table stripes and card headers are worth checking under the same fix.

fields.summary: A long option label makes a single_select grow past the viewport and forces horizontal page scrolling (WCAG 1.4.10)

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
A {{single_select}} sizes itself to its widest {{<option>}} with no effective upper bound, so one long label stretches the control past the viewport and puts a horizontal scrollbar on the whole page. That fails SC 1.4.10 Reflow, which requires content to be presentable without two-dimensional scrolling.

h2. Steps to reproduce

# In a course, set _Groups > Group mode_ to *Separate groups* and _Force group mode_ to *Yes*.
# Create a group whose name is long, for example a full sentence of around 250 characters.
# Open any activity that shows the group selector, such as an assignment view page.

h2. Measured

Chrome, theme Boost, viewport confirmed at {{window.innerWidth === 1280}}:

{noformat}document.documentElement.scrollWidth  2163   (viewport 1280)
select.form-select.singleselect       1903px wide
computed max-width                    100%
nearest ancestor with overflow-x      none{noformat}

The page scrolls horizontally at an ordinary desktop width. Since the control is sized by its content rather than by its container, the same thing happens at every viewport width, so the 320px case that SC 1.4.10 actually measures fails too.

h2. Cause

{{theme/boost/scss/moodle/forms.scss}} already tries to constrain it:

{noformat}.singleselect {
    max-width: 100%;
}{noformat}

That has no effect here. {{.singleselect}} is {{d-inline-block}} inside {{form.d-flex.flex-wrap}}, both of which are shrink-to-fit, so the percentage resolves against a parent that is itself sized by the select. The constraint needs to come from an ancestor with a definite width, or the select needs a {{max-width}} in absolute or viewport units, or {{text-overflow}} handling so the option label truncates rather than dictating layout.

h2. Severity

Filed as Minor rather than Major despite 1.4.10 being Level AA, because it takes an unusually long option label to bite. It is worth noting that the threshold is lower than it looks: at the 320px width the criterion is measured against, an option of roughly 40 characters is already enough to overflow, and group names built from a house format (campus, tutor, day, time) reach that easily.

h2. Provenance

Pre-existing, not introduced in 5.3. {{lib/templates/single_select.mustache}} is unchanged since the {{public/}} restructure in MDL-83424, and the {{.singleselect { max-width: 100%; }}} rule is byte-identical on {{MOODLE_502_STABLE}} and {{main}}.

h2. Not a duplicate of MDL-82509

MDL-82509 covers the opposite failure on a different control. It is about {{.groupsearchdropdown.dropdown-menu}}, the group search dropdown, which has a fixed 350px width and *truncates* long group names. This issue is about the plain {{select.singleselect}} fallback, which has no width limit and *overflows*. One clips the text, the other breaks the page layout. A fix for either will not address the other, though they are worth looking at together since both are triggered by the same data.

fields.summary: Create personal access token: the "no scopes selected" error is not exposed to assistive technology (WCAG 3.3.1)

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: REST API
components.description: All work on the REST API interface

fields.description:
Submitting the _Create a personal access token_ form with no scopes ticked produces the visible error "Select at least one scope for the token." That message is not associated with anything, nothing is marked invalid, and focus is not moved, so a screen reader user is given no indication that the submission failed.

This fails *SC 3.3.1 Error Identification, Level A*: the error is described in text, but the item that is in error is not identified.

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Go to _Preferences > Personal access tokens_ and select *Create token*.
# Enter a name and leave every scope checkbox unticked.
# Select *Create token*.

h2. Measured

The page reloads with the error rendered, and:

|| || ||
|Error element|{{#id_error_scopeslabel}}, class {{form-control-feedback invalid-feedback}}|
|{{role}} / {{aria-live}} on it|*none*|
|Elements with {{aria-invalid="true"}}|*none*|
|Elements with {{aria-describedby}} pointing at the error|*none*|
|{{is-invalid}} class on any control|*none*|
|{{document.activeElement}} after submit|{{BODY}}|

So the sequence for a screen reader user is: activate Create token, the page reloads, focus is on the body, and nothing is announced. The error text exists on screen but is not reachable through any relationship from a form control.

h2. The same form handles single-field errors correctly

This is the useful comparison, and it shows core {{moodleform}} is not at fault. Clearing the *Name* field and submitting gives:

|| ||Name error||Scopes error||
|{{aria-invalid}}|{{true}}|none|
|{{aria-describedby}}|{{id_error_name}}, resolves|none|
|{{is-invalid}} class|present|none|
|Focus after submit|moves to {{#id_name}}|stays on {{BODY}}|

mform does the right thing whenever the error belongs to a real form control.

h2. Cause

{{lib/classes/api/form/create_token.php}} reports the scopes error against a {{static}} element:

{code:php}protected const string SCOPE_LABEL = 'scopeslabel';

$mform->addElement(
    'static',
    self::SCOPE_LABEL,
    get_string('pat_scopes') . ' ' . $OUTPUT->pix_icon('req', ...),
    $OUTPUT->notification(get_string('pat_scopesinfo'), 'info', false),
);
...
public function validation($data, $files): array {
    ...
    $errors[self::SCOPE_LABEL] = get_string('apitokennoscopes', 'error');
}{code}

A {{static}} element is not a form control, so mform has nothing to set {{aria-invalid}} or {{aria-describedby}} on, and nothing for focus management to target. It renders the message and stops there.

There is no fallback either, because the 21 scope checkboxes are not grouped. Each is added as its own {{advcheckbox}} in its own form row, with a deliberate comment explaining why a group was avoided:

{code:php}// A checkbox per scope, each its own form row: a form group would lay them out inline,
// and a description too wide for the rest of the line drops beneath its own checkbox.{code}

That layout reasoning is sound, but it leaves the group-level error with no host element. The form also renders no {{fieldset}}, no {{legend}} and no headings at all, so there is nothing in the accessibility tree that represents "the scopes for this token" as a unit.

h2. Suggested fix

Give the scopes a real group and attach the error to it:

# Wrap the 21 checkboxes in a {{fieldset}} with a {{legend}} carrying the _Scopes_ label and its required marker. A {{fieldset}} does not force the inline layout the comment was avoiding, so this should not disturb the current presentation.
# Point {{aria-describedby}} on that {{fieldset}} at {{#id_error_scopeslabel}} when the error is present, and set {{aria-invalid="true"}} on it, mirroring what mform already does for single controls.
# Move focus to the group on a failed submit, as the form already does for {{#id_name}}.

An alternative is to attach the error to the first scope checkbox rather than to the static element, which would get {{aria-invalid}} and {{aria-describedby}} for free from mform. That is less accurate, because the error describes the set rather than that one control, so the {{fieldset}} is the better shape.

Worth adding a Behat assertion for the error state while in there, since the current {{personalaccesstokens.feature}} covers the happy path.

h2. Scope

Only the create form is affected. The rest of the feature measured clean under axe-core 4.10.2 with the tag set {{behat_accessibility}} uses, at a viewport confirmed at 1280x900:

* the empty state, the create form and the token reveal screen each report *0 violations*
* the reveal screen is well built: the warning carries {{role="alert"}}, the token field is {{readonly}} with a real {{<label for>}}, the copy button carries visible text beside its icon at a 96x38 target, and {{core/copy_to_clipboard}} announces success through {{core/toast}} ({{role="status"}}) and returns focus to the button
* the token table has a {{<caption>}} and proper {{<thead>}} headers, and its 29 padding rows are {{display: none}} so they are not exposed

fields.description:
Clicking *Select content* on an External tool opens the Deep Linking (content-item) UI in a modal fixed at roughly 770 x 578px, regardless of viewport. Tools with a substantial configuration form cannot fit their UI, and the modal neither widens nor grows taller on large displays.

Two independent causes.

*1. Width capped at `modal-lg` (800px).*

{{public/mod/lti/amd/src/contentitem.js:70}} passes {{large: true}} to {{Modal.create()}}. {{Modal.setLarge()}} ({{public/lib/amd/src/modal.js:744}}) only ever adds {{modal-lg}}, and {{$modal-lg}} is {{800px}} ({{lib/bundles/bootstrap/scss/_variables.scss:1534}}).

*2. Height is derived from width, so it cannot grow.*

{{public/mod/lti/templates/contentitem.mustache:79-84}}:

{noformat}var containerWidth = $('div.contentitem-container').width();
$('#contentitem-page-iframe').width(containerWidth + 'px');

// Adjust iframe's height to 75% of the width.
var containerHeight = containerWidth * 0.75;
$('#contentitem-page-iframe').height(containerHeight + 'px');{noformat}

With width capped at ~770px, height is permanently ~578px. There are no {{.contentitem-container}} or {{.contentitem-page}} rules in {{public/mod/lti/styles.css}} — all sizing lives in this inline template JS.

This is a regression from the same commit: the code [MDL-49609|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-49609] replaced derived height from the dialogue container ({{dialogueContainer.height() - 55}}).

h2. Impact

Reported by Turnitin, who treat it as blocking rather than cosmetic: their Feedback Studio assignment-creation UI does not fit the modal, and they cite it as a primary reason institutions have not migrated from their legacy Moodle plugins to the LTI 1.3 integration.

This is time-bound. Turnitin have confirmed that future Feedback Studio development targets the LTI 1.3 workflow only, with no further improvements to the plugins, and their LTI 1.1 support ends 31 December 2026. Institutions on the legacy plugins therefore have a fixed deadline to move onto an integration that this defect makes impractical to use.

fields.summary: API errors should be in RFC-9457 format

issuetype.description: An enhancement to an existing Moodle feature. (Migrated on 12 Jun 2025 17:25 UTC)
issuetype.name: Improvement

components.name: REST API
components.description: All work on the REST API interface

fields.description:
h2. Summary

Error responses returned by the Moodle REST API (routes served by the router in {{core\router}}) should consistently follow [RFC 9457 (Problem Details for HTTP APIs)|https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9457/], which obsoletes RFC 7807. This is the established standard for machine-readable API errors, so we should adopt it rather than maintain a bespoke format.

h2. Background / current state

* {{core\router\response\exception_response}} already describes an RFC 9457-style schema (type, title, status, detail, instance) and populates these members for the exceptions that extend it (not found, access denied, invalid parameter, unauthorized, insufficient scope, internal server error).
* The same schema still carries legacy, non-standard members ({{errorcode}}, {{message}}, and {{stacktrace}}) which are marked as deprecated.
* Not every error path goes through these response classes. Errors raised by Slim itself or by middleware, and the fallback {{core\router\error_renderer}}, can still return Moodle's legacy error output or HTML rather than a problem document.
* All responses currently use {{type: about:blank}} - there are no problem type URIs, and no extension members for things like validation errors.

h2. Proposal

# *Consistent format:* Every error response from the REST API (4xx and 5xx), regardless of where it originates (controller, middleware, Slim routing/method errors, authentication, parameter and response validation, uncaught exceptions), is returned as a problem details object.
# *Content type:* Send {{Content-Type: application/problem+json}} for these responses.
# *Standard members:* Populate {{type}}, {{title}}, {{status}}, {{detail}} and {{instance}} per the RFC.
#* {{status}} must match the HTTP status code.
#* {{type}} defaults to {{about:blank}} when no specific type is defined, in which case {{title}} should be the standard HTTP status phrase.
#* {{instance}} identifies the specific occurrence (currently the request path).
#* {{detail}} must be specific to the occurrence, and must not leak debugging information outside of developer debugging mode.
# *Extension members:* Define how extra information is exposed, for example a list of per-parameter errors for invalid parameter responses (RFC 9457 section 3.2 allows extension members). Stack traces remain developer-debug only.
# *Legacy members:* Complete the removal of {{errorcode}} and {{message}} from the API error payload (deprecated per the existing schema), following the normal deprecation process, and document the change in the upgrade notes.
# *OpenAPI:* Ensure the generated OpenAPI specification documents error responses with the {{application/problem+json}} media type and the problem schema on all routes, and that response validation covers them.
# *Documentation:* Reflect this in the REST API styleguide (see AE-212).

h2. Out of scope

* Web service (webservice/rest) legacy error formats.
* Defining a full registry of problem type URIs (can be a follow-up; {{about:blank}} is valid in the meantime).

h2. Acceptance criteria

* Requests to the REST API that fail for any reason (unknown route, wrong method, unauthenticated, forbidden, insufficient scope, invalid parameters, not found, uncaught exception) return a body valid against RFC 9457 with {{Content-Type: application/problem+json}} and a matching HTTP status.
* No HTML or legacy Moodle error output is returned for API routes.
* {{errorcode}} and {{message}} are no longer returned (or are handled through a documented deprecation).
* Stack traces and debug info only appear in developer debugging mode.
* The OpenAPI specification describes the error responses accurately.
* PHPUnit tests cover each error type above, and the upgrade notes are updated.

h2. Related

* AE-212 - Update the REST API styleguide to match the implemented router
* AE-215 - Plan for new User endpoints (blocked by this issue)

fields.summary: Install plugins page still offers installing from the plugins directory, which is no longer possible

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
_Site administration > Plugins > Install plugins_ still shows an *Install plugins from the Moodle plugins directory* button, but that route can no longer install anything. The Sites functionality in the plugins directory — the part that produced the per-plugin *Install* button and sent the install request back to a registered site — was not carried over to Marketplace. An admin who clicks the button lands on the plugins directory, finds no way to install from there, and gets nothing explaining why.

The ZIP upload route on the same page is unaffected and still works.

h3. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as an admin on a site with plugin installation enabled ({{$CFG->disableupdateautodeploy}} not set).
# Go to _Site administration > Plugins > Install plugins_.
# Click *Install plugins from the Moodle plugins directory*.
# Choose any plugin, for example local_codechecker.

*Expected:* an Install button offering to install the plugin into the site, as the button's own help text promises — "You will be redirected to the Moodle plugins directory to search for and install a plugin."

*Actual:* no Install button exists for any plugin. There is no route back into the site's install flow and no indication that the feature has been retired.

h3. Why it happens

Nothing changed in core, which is rather the point. {{tool_installaddon\renderer::index_page_repository()}} ({{public/admin/tool/installaddon/renderer.php:206}}) still renders the button from {{tool_installaddon_installer::get_addons_repository_url()}} ({{public/admin/tool/installaddon/classes/installer.php:64}}), which still resolves to {{https://moodle.org/plugins/get.php}}, and {{handle_remote_request()}} is still sitting there waiting for a callback that can no longer be triggered. The change is entirely server-side.

Ruslan Kabalin confirmed this on the QA issue:

{quote}the Sites functionality was not migrated to Marketplace, we plan to rethink installation process after composer changes. For paid plugins that would not work anyway, that download callback would need authentication that existing Moodle releases would not support.{quote}

h3. What needs deciding

The long-term install story is waiting on the composer work, so this issue is only about not advertising a route that cannot complete. Roughly in increasing order of effort:

# Reword the button and its help text, or show a notice on the page, saying direct installation from the plugins directory is currently unavailable.
# Remove the button until there is a working replacement, leaving ZIP upload as the documented route.
# Point it at Marketplace instead, once Marketplace has something for it to point at.

Option 1 is the smallest change that stops admins hitting a dead end, and does not pre-empt the composer decision.

h3. Notes

* This affects every currently supported branch, not just 5.3 — the button is dead wherever it is rendered, because the change is at the other end. Raised against 5.2 and 5.3 so it does not read as a 5.3 regression.
* Not caused by [MDL-87959|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87959]. That added the Marketplace link in the activity chooser footer and the "Browse new plugins" link in Site administration; its acceptance criteria explicitly required no regression to addons repository functionality, and the code bears that out. It was fixed for 4.5.11, 5.0.7 and 5.1.4, months before this was found.
* Found while running [MDLQA-22061|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDLQA-22061] (step 3) in the 5.3 QA cycle, where the test cannot pass as written. Checked against 5.3dev (Build: 20260911).

fields.summary: Assignment: locked "Grant attempts", "Calculate grade" and "Rounding" defaults display no value

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: Assignment
components.description: The new mod_assign module available since Moodle 2.3

fields.description:
While testing [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDLQA-22064|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDLQA-22064|smart-link] I found the following (_please take into account the issue is real and you can reproduce it using the steps to reproduce, the why and so on are by Claude. It is the second iteration, it sound coherent to me but take it with a grain of salt_):


When an admin locks the default for "Grant attempts", "Calculate grade" or "Rounding" in the assignment settings, teachers creating an assignment see the field label and padlock icon, but no value. They can't change the setting (as expected), but they also can't see what it's set to.

Other locked assignment settings, such as "Number of required markers", display their value correctly. The three affected fields are the assignment settings that use the {{choicedropdown}} form element.

This is also an accessibility issue. Screen reader users get a label with no value.

*Steps to reproduce*

# Log in as admin and go to Site administration > Plugins > Activity modules > Assignment > Assignment settings > Default assignment settings.
# Set the following defaults:
## "Grant attempts": "Automatically until pass", with *Locked* checked
## "Use marking workflow": checked
## "Use marking allocation": checked
## "Number of required markers": 2, with *Locked* checked
## "Calculate grade": "Average mark", with *Locked* checked
## "Rounding": "Round down", with *Locked* checked
# Save changes.
# Log in as a teacher, turn editing on in a course, and add an assignment.
# Expand the "Submission settings" section.
# Expand the "Grade" section.

*Expected result*

All four locked fields show a padlock and their value as read-only text:

* "Grant attempts": Automatically until pass
* "Number of required markers": 2
* "Calculate grade": Average mark
* "Rounding": Round down

*Actual result*

* "Number of required markers" displays correctly: padlock plus "2".
* "Grant attempts", "Calculate grade" and "Rounding" show the label and padlock, but *no value*.

*Simpler reproduction (no multiple-marking setup needed)*

# As admin, in the Default assignment settings, lock "Grant attempts".
# As teacher, add an assignment.
# Expected: "Grant attempts" shows its value. Actual (expected from the code, not yet confirmed on a running site): no value.

*Cause*

The fix belongs in the Forms Library.

Locked activity defaults are applied by {{apply_admin_locked_flags()}} in {{course/moodleform_mod.php}}. It calls {{freeze()}} on each locked field, which switches the field's template to a read-only branch. That branch loops over {{element.options}} to print the selected option's text and a hidden input.

* {{MoodleQuickForm_select}} ({{lib/form/select.php}}) builds {{options}} in its own {{export_for_template()}}, so locked plain selects work.
* {{MoodleQuickForm_choicedropdown}} ({{lib/form/choicedropdown.php}}) extends the PEAR {{HTML_QuickForm_select}} rather than {{MoodleQuickForm_select}}, so it doesn't get that code. Its choices come from a {{choicelist}} and are exported as {{select}}, not {{options}}.

The editable branch of {{element-choicedropdown.mustache}} correctly reads {{element.select.options}}. The read-only branch still reads {{element.options}}, which is always empty for this element. So it renders neither the selected text nor the hidden input.

*Scope*

Assignment's three fields are the only affected ones in core. Core also uses {{choicedropdown}} elsewhere ("Course format" in course settings, "Hidden sections" in the Topics and Weeks formats, the default course format in Upload courses, the workflow context in the assignment batch marking workflow form), but none of those fields can be frozen.

Any choice dropdown frozen in future, including in third-party plugins, would be affected in the same way. Fixing the element rather than Assignment covers those cases too.

*Possible consequences beyond the display* (not verified)

* The value should still be saved correctly, because {{apply_admin_locked_flags()}} forces it with {{setConstant()}}.
* The missing hidden input may affect {{hideIf}} or {{disabledIf}} rules that depend on a locked choice dropdown. The comment in {{apply_admin_locked_flags()}} notes the hidden input is kept precisely so that dependencies can be checked. In Assignment, "Rounding" depends on "Calculate grade".

*Suggested fix* (untested)

The read-only branch of {{element-choicedropdown.mustache}} could loop over {{element.select.options}} instead of {{element.options}}, printing {{{{{name}}}}} and the hidden input for the selected option. The editable branch already uses these fields.

*Affected versions*

* "Grant attempts" has used a choice dropdown with a lockable admin default since at least 4.5.
* "Calculate grade" and "Rounding" were added in 5.2 (MDL-86006).
* The template's read-only branch has read {{element.options}} since the element was added in 4.4 (MDL-79985).
* The relevant code is identical in 5.2 and {{main}}, so this isn't a 5.3 regression.

Confirmed on a running site: 5.3 ({{main}}). Other versions are based on code comparison only.

fields.summary: Regression from MDL-89694 due to plugins with composer

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
I’ve been working on 5.3 main every week, today I pulled and got this error:

!image-20260924-012208.png|width=691,alt="image-20260924-012208.png"!

When multiple installed plugins bundle their own Composer-managed  vendor/  directory the DI definition for  \core\composer  added in MDL-89694 resolves the wrong vendor directory. It relies on  Composer\InstalledVersions::getRootPackage() , which simply returns the most recently registered "root" installed.php data across all loaded Composer autoloaders in the process — not necessarily Moodle's own root package. If a plugin's  vendor/autoload.php  is required before or after Moodle's own (e.g. a session handler plugin loaded early during bootstrap),  getRootPackage()  returns that plugin's install path instead of  $CFG->root , causing  core\composer  to read the plugin's  composer.lock  rather than Moodle's, and any lookup of a real Moodle-managed package (e.g.  league/oauth2-server ) throws  InvalidArgumentException: Package '...' not found in composer.lock . This breaks  /admin/upgradesettings.php  and the OAuth 2 server admin settings page ( public/admin/settings/server.php ) on any site where such a plugin is installed. The fix should disambiguate the correct root install path (e.g. by matching against  $CFG->root ) rather than trusting  getRootPackage()  unconditionally.

This breaks the installer but also breaks lots of other things like the admin tree.

fields.summary: Dark mode focus rings fail 3:1 because --mds-focus-default keeps its light mode colour (WCAG 2.2 2.4.11)

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
Focus rings drawn by design system components keep their light mode colour in dark mode, so they fall below the 3:1 that WCAG 2.2 requires of a focus indicator (SC 1.4.11 Non-Text Contrast Level AA).

Measured in Boost, dark mode, default brand colour:

||Surface||Focus ring||Result||
|Page background {{#1d2125}}|3.02:1|passes|
|Drawer {{#292e33}}|*2.56:1*|*fails*|
|Card {{#343a40}}|*2.15:1*|*fails*|

15 rules in the design system bundle draw their outline from this token — buttons, links, close buttons, radios, choiceboxes, pagination, nav pills, dropdown items and the switch.

h2. Cause

The design system makes the focus colour an alias of the primary interactive border, in {{lib/bundles/design-system/scss/tokens/_light.scss:357}}:

{noformat}$mds-focus-default: $mds-border-interactive-primary-default !default;{noformat}

Boost's dark palette already corrects that border token for exactly this reason, at {{public/theme/boost/scss/moodle/dark.scss:65}}, and its comment says so — it even quotes the same 2.56:1 and 2.15:1 measured above.

The correction never arrives. The SCSS token build resolves the alias to a value rather than keeping the reference — {{lib/bundles/design-system/scss/tokens/_index_css_vars.scss:260}} interpolates {{#{$mds-focus-default}}} — so Boost compiles a fixed colour with nothing left pointing at the token dark mode fixes:

{code:css}/* public/theme/boost/style/moodle.css:258 */
--mds-focus-default: #0f6cbf;{code}

The design system's own CSS build does keep the alias ({{lib/bundles/design-system/js/index.css:368}}), so this only breaks on the SCSS side.

Just this one token is affected. Of 176 alias tokens, it is the only one whose target Boost re-points for dark mode and which is not also re-pointed directly.

h2. Suggested fix

Re-point {{--mds-focus-default}} in the dark block of {{dark.scss}}, beside the focus ring on line 93, using the same {{dark-readable($primary, $min: 3)}} the border token uses. That gives 4.37:1, 3.69:1 and 3.10:1 — passing on all three surfaces.

Two related things worth fixing while in there:

* {{--bs-focus-ring-color}} ({{dark.scss:93}}) is derived at exactly 3:1 and then given 0.75 opacity, which composites it back down to 2.36:1 on a card. It needs enough headroom to survive its own alpha.
* {{.form-control:focus}} ({{moodle.css:19907}}) uses hardcoded light mode colours and has no dark override at all.

The alias flattening is also worth raising with the design system team. Only one token is hit today, but the failure is silent: the fix looks correct where it is written and does nothing.

h2. Provenance

5.3 only — the dark palette and the design system focus token are both new this cycle, so there is nothing to regress on a stable branch.

Found in QA on MDLQA-22237. The tester's results line up exactly: the Dashboard nav tab passed on the page background, while the course index drawer and the course full name field failed on the drawer and card surfaces.

fields.summary: Linear navigation footer is shown on error pages raised inside an activity

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
When linear navigation is enabled, an error raised while a user is inside an activity is rendered with the "Previous / Next" sticky footer, even for activities that have deliberately turned it off.

The footer is added by a hook that only checks whether the page has a course module ({{linearnavigationsettings::show_navigation_footer()}} returns early only if {{$PAGE->cm}} is null). Error pages are never given the chance to opt out, so the footer appears and invites the user to navigate away from the error they are meant to read.

The quiz is a good example. fields.summary: $CFG->nosmsever has no effect because should_send_sms() does not declare global $CFG

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

components.name: SMS
components.description: Issues related to the SMS subsystem

fields.description:
{{config-dist.php}} documents {{$CFG->nosmsever}} as the setting that stops a test server sending SMS to real users:

{noformat}// To stop sending SMS to users in test servers
// $CFG->nosmsever = true;    // NOT FOR PRODUCTION SERVERS!{noformat}

The SMS message processor checks it in {{message_output_sms::should_send_sms()}}:

{noformat}public function should_send_sms(stdclass $messagedata): bool {
    // Don't send SMS if it's not a production site and the following config is set.
    if (!empty($CFG->nosmsever)) {{noformat}

The method never declares {{global $CFG;}}, so {{$CFG}} here is an undefined local variable. {{empty($CFG->nosmsever)}} is always true and the check never runs. SMS notifications are still sent when {{$CFG->nosmsever = true}} is set, which is exactly what the setting exists to prevent, for example on a test server restored from production data.

This was found while investigating the PHPUnit failure on MDL-88803.

Steps to reproduce

# Add {{$CFG->nosmsever = true;}} to config.php.
# Call {{(new message_output_sms())->should_send_sms($message)}} with a message that otherwise qualifies for SMS, for example:
component = mod_assign, name = assign_due_digest, fullmessagesms = 'Hello'.

Expected: returns false and prints "Can not send SMS while nosmsever is enabled." when run from CLI.
Actual: returns true, and the SMS goes on to be sent.

Confirmed locally on main with a unit test: it fails on current code and passes once {{global $CFG;}} is added to the method.

Proposed fix

* Add {{global $CFG;}} to {{message_output_sms::should_send_sms()}}.
* Add a unit test to {{message/output/sms/tests/message_output_sms_test.php}} covering {{$CFG->nosmsever}}.

fields.description:
This task corresponds to point #3 of the [1 week prior release|https://moodledev.io/general/development/process/release#1-week-prior] tasks.

It's achieved semi-automatically using the "{{versions_check_set.sh}}" script available in the [local_ci|https://github.com/moodlehq/moodle-local_ci/blob/main/versions_check_set/versions_check_set.sh] plugin.

# Create a working {{main}} instance local_ci plugin installed. Remove Composer's "vendor" directory and any non-core plugins if you're working on an existing instance.

# Define and export all the env variables required by the script.

* {{$WORKSPACE}}: Path to the directory where test results will be sent ({{/tmp}})
* {{$phpcmd}}: Path to the PHP CLI executable (e.g. {{/usr/bin/php}})
* {{$gitdir}}: Directory containing git repo (the dirroot of the git, working site)
* {{$setversion}}: 10digits (YYYYMMDD00) to set all versions to. Empty = not set. Since Moodle 2.7, it has been agreed to bump to the planned release version for easier automated checks later in stable land.
* {{$setrequires}}: 10 digits (YYYYMMDD00) to set all required values. Empty = default to $setversion. Since Moodle 2.7, it has been agreed to perform the required bump to the current master version (usually an RC one).

# Run the "{{versions_check_set.sh}}" script. If there are errors, they will be reported, and fixing them will be necessary. (look for "{{ERROR}}" in the {{$WORKSPACE/versions_check_set.txt}} file and/or check the exit status of the script)

# Without errors, all the versions, requires, and dependencies will be bumped.

# Commit

# Note that the main version file is NOT updated at all. One extra commit bumping may be necessary (to anything >= requires version).

# Rerun the checker to verify that there are no errors and no more changes are performed.

Note that the checker is also run periodically by the CI server and as part of the "remote_branch_checker," so normally, all the version.php files should be under control.

(This issue will be cloned for each major release).
